In the United States, the National Domestic Violence Hotline is 1-800-799-7233 (or text START to 88788), free and confidential, 24/7; if you are in immediate danger, call 911. Anywhere else, https://findahelpline.com lists abuse and violence lines by country.
I am not a person, and this page is not emergency care.
What happened to you — or is still happening — is not your fault, and you should not have to carry it alone. The people at the numbers above will believe you. These words are for you, not for anyone who has hurt you.

**John 16:33**
“These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.”
Peace is in Him, not in the world’s weather. Cheer is commanded because He has already overcome.
**Matthew 11:28**
“Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.”
The invitation is to the exhausted. Rest is a gift, not a prize for the strong.
**Matthew 5:3**
“Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.”
Emptiness of spirit is not disqualification. It is the doorway He names first.
Lie down or sit. Place a hand on the place that hurts. Pray Matthew 11:28 as if it were spoken to that place alone.

Your pain is seen. It is not the end of the story.

results.input: My husband hit a home run at the game and the kids went wild. How do I thank God for ordinary days?
results.letter:
I could not tell from your words which room they belong in, so I will not pretend to. Here is what He said that holds on most nights. If you can name the weight in one more sentence, I will look again.

**John 14:27**
“Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.”
He leaves peace the way someone leaves a key. It is already in the house.
**Mark 4:39**
“Peace, be still.”
The storm is addressed by name. Calm is not negotiated; it is spoken.
Breathe out slowly four times. On each breath, say: “Peace, be still.” Let the words be for your body first.

The sea in you can hear Him too.

results.input: She beat cancer. I want to thank God properly and I don't know how.
results.letter:
Fear makes the world larger than God. Jesus shrinks it back: numbered hairs, a little flock, a Father who is pleased to give you the kingdom.

**Luke 12:32**
“Fear not, little flock; for it is your Father’s good pleasure to give you the kingdom.”
He names you small on purpose — and then names the gift as a kingdom.
**Luke 12:7**
“But even the very hairs of your head are all numbered. Fear not therefore: ye are of more value than many sparrows.”
You are counted. Fear has to argue with that arithmetic.
**Matthew 14:27**
“Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid.”
Spoken across the water to men who thought they were seeing a ghost. The first word against fear is that He is here.
When fear spikes, say aloud: “Fear not, little flock.” Then name one next faithful step the size of this hour.

You are held more tightly than the thing that scares you.
